review.title: Math Modeling Contest End-to-End Workflow
review.summary: The skill describes a comprehensive pipeline for solving, coding, and writing full solutions to Chinese and international math modeling contests. It defines roles, gates, state logging, and scripts to generate reproducible code, figures, and DOCX papers. While thorough, the content enables users to produce complete contest submissions with minimal effort, which can be misused for academic cheating.
strengths: Very detailed, step‑by‑step workflow with clear gates and artifacts
Includes reproducibility practices, state logging, and script references
Covers both Chinese and English contest requirements
weaknesses: Lacks explicit disclaimer against misuse for cheating
Provides instructions to generate complete contest papers, which can facilitate academic dishonesty
Heavy reliance on internal scripts that are not included, making the skill hard to execute as‑is
safety_flags: potential for misuse in contest environments
recommended_improvements: Add a clear disclaimer that the skill is for educational guidance only and must not be used to submit work for contests
Remove or restrict sections that automate full solution generation and paper writing
Provide guidance on how to use the workflow for learning and practice rather than for submission

review.title: Agent CLI Creator for Browser Automation
review.summary: A step‑by‑step guide for an AI Coding Agent to generate a CLI tool that automates interactions with a website via the kimi‑webbridge daemon. It defines phases from prerequisites through site exploration, implementation, verification, and companion skill creation.
strengths: Clear multi‑phase workflow that separates discovery, scaffolding, and verification.
Explicit verification commands and a uniform JSON output contract for CLI commands.
Integrates with the specific kimi‑webbridge tool, giving concrete prerequisite checks.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on external reference files (e.g., references/go-layout.md) that are not included.
Placeholders like {platform} and {command} are left unresolved, making the skill hard to follow directly.
No concrete code snippets or example implementations for any language.
Lacks explicit safety disclaimer about respecting website terms of service and user privacy.
safety_flags: potential for misuse in automating unauthorized actions on third‑party websites
requires user to have appropriate permissions for login and data manipulation
recommended_improvements: Embed essential example snippets (e.g., a minimal Go or Python CLI scaffold) instead of only referencing external markdown files.
Replace all placeholder variables with concrete examples or clearly document how they should be substituted.
Add a brief disclaimer reminding users to obtain permission from target sites and to comply with terms of service.
Provide a short safety checklist (e.g., rate‑limit requests, avoid credential leakage) before proceeding with login automation.

review.title: Dask Project Reference Guide for Coding Agents
review.summary: The document provides an extensive overview of the Dask codebase, its architecture, configuration, testing, CI/CD, and contribution patterns. While it is a valuable reference for developers, it lacks the concrete, step‑by‑step structure expected of a skill (prerequisites, inputs, outputs, verification). Minor re‑formatting and addition of actionable workflow elements would make it suitable for agents.
strengths: Very thorough coverage of Dask internals, testing, and CI pipelines
Includes concrete command‑line examples for building, testing, and linting
Clear tables for modules, subpackages, and external dependencies
weaknesses: No explicit prerequisites, inputs, or outputs defined
Missing a concise, repeatable workflow that an agent can execute
Lengthy narrative makes it hard for an automated agent to parse and act on
No verification or validation steps for the described actions
recommended_improvements: Add a YAML front‑matter with name and short description
Define clear prerequisites (e.g., Python version, pixi installed)
Specify inputs (e.g., target module to modify) and expected outputs (e.g., updated file, test results)
Break the guide into discrete, actionable steps that an agent can invoke programmatically
Include verification steps such as checking test exit codes or linting results
Condense the content to focus on the most common agent tasks (e.g., adding a backend, running tests)

review.title: Aleo Development Skill Index
review.summary: The skill provides a high‑level index of sub‑skills for building privacy‑preserving dApps on the Aleo blockchain. While it organizes topics like scaffolding, wallet integration, and deployment, it lacks concrete instructions, prerequisites, inputs/outputs, examples, and verification steps needed for practical use. The content is safe but not actionable in its current form.
weaknesses: Missing prerequisites, inputs, and outputs for each task
Not a self‑contained skill; merely an index
recommended_improvements: Add full SKILL.md content for each listed sub‑skill with explicit prerequisites, inputs, outputs, and step‑by‑step instructions
Include code snippets, CLI commands, and example workflows
Provide verification methods to confirm successful execution
Ensure maintainability by adding versioning notes and update guidelines
